title: Off-rank stalk vanishing of pulled-back Koszul Ext
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], let $\mathcal I$ be its kernel ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $C=i^*\mathcal I$ be its tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Use the derived category and derived internal Hom of [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and write $F^q=H^q(R\mathcal Hom_Y(i_*\mathcal O_Z,\mathcal O_Y))$. Suppose near every $z\in Z$ an affine neighbourhood of $i(z)$ cuts out $i$ by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let $r:Z\to\mathbb N$ be locally constant with $r(z)=\operatorname{finrank}_{\mathcal O_{Z,z}}C_z$, where the module stalk is [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. For every $q\in\mathbb Z$ and $z\in Z$ with $q\ne r(z)$, the stalk $(i^*F^q)_z$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, Koszul cohomology calculation and local comparison

proof.text: Choose an affine Koszul chart U at i(z), with sequence f of length n. The regular conormal basis gives a basis of (i.ker.ideal U).Cotangent. The affine conormal frame identifies the conormal stalk finrank at z with n. Compose with hr to obtain r(z)=n, and rewrite hq to q≠n.

In the standard derived category of modules over A=Γ(Y,U), choose the normalized dual Koszul comparison and apply its cohomology theorem to q≠n. This proves that the actual integer-indexed dual Koszul homology module in degree q is zero, including negative q.

Apply affine_koszul_scalar_ext_comparison to identify F^q.over U with the transported associated sheaf of this homology module. Tilde, restriction along the affine isomorphism, and the inverse over-site equivalence preserve zero morphisms and hence zero objects. Transport through the comparison to prove F^q.over U is zero.

Represent each element of the stalk of F^q at i(z) by a germ on V and restrict to V∩U. Applying id=0 for F^q.over U to this restricted section makes it zero. Germ restriction compatibility then proves each original germ is zero, hence the stalk module is a zero object. Use the tensor-pullback stalk isomorphism and preservation of zero objects by extension of scalars to conclude that (i^*F^q)_z is zero.
